text.p: Zaire's prime minister, in Europe to discuss the conflict in eastern Zaire, has made a brief visit to Switzerland where his president Mobutu Sese Seko, stricken by cancer, is being treated, Swiss news agency ATS said on Friday.

The agency said Kengo wa Dondo flew into Geneva on Thursday evening from Brussels where he had met European Union special envoy for the Great Lakes region, Aldo Ajello. It said Kengo left Geneva later the same evening.

Zairean embassy in Geneva declined to comment and it was not clear whether Kongo visited Mobutu, who is receiving chemotherapy in Lausanne, 60 km (37 miles) east of Geneva, where he underwent surgery for prostate cancer on August 22.

Some 300,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees are on the run in eastern Zaire fleeing clashes between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsis and concern is growing about the future of the vast, anarchic Central African country if Mobutu dies.
Swiss authorities on Thursday extended Mobutu's visa on humanitarian grounds -- for the third time in two months -- but would not say when it would expire.
